title: Release Flow: Guided Canary & Fallback First-Run Visual Kit
creator: Nora Chen
description: Create a compact visual kit and annotated screenshots for the first-time release flow that walks engineers through canarying a model version, setting A/B splits, and configuring fallback policies. Deliverables include responsive screenshots for desktop and mobile, an interactive percentage slider mock, a simulated traffic heatmap, and a short explainer panel for deterministic version locking ("model lock"). These assets will be used on the quickstart page, onboarding modal, and the docs landing for Release Flow.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Desktop and mobile screenshots covering: canary percentage slider, A/B variant chooser, deterministic model lock modal, fallback policy dropdown and explanation, and final rollout summary screen.
A2: Annotated Figma frames with copy notes for engineer-friendly language and localization hints (EN + example for DE).
A3: Lightweight interaction prototype for the canary slider and fallback selector that product can demo in onboarding sessions.
A4: Exported PNGs and a single compressed sprite for the quickstart guide; image names must match docs import spec.
A5: Accessibility checks: contrast ratios documented and keyboard flows for slider and variant picker described.
A6: Design review completed and PM sign-off recorded in comments with link to Confluence PRD.
design_notes: Keep the visual language consistent with Console 2025 theme: rounded chips, 12px label type, 16px body.
Replace generic 'rollout' term in UI copy with 'Release Flow' to reduce ambiguity for teams using both Dedicated and Private environments.
Use explicit numeric percentages (0%, 5%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 100%) as preset stops for the slider plus manual entry for exact control.
Include 'preview traffic' toggle that simulates 1 minute of traffic distribution using customer config to validate routing rules.
Fallback policy UI should present three succinct options: 'Failover to latest stable', 'Failover to pinned version', 'Return error with webhook' (each with short one-line explanation).
Design to avoid deep modal stacks; prefer in-panel progressive disclosure for variant details.
Provide a compact summary chip showing estimated token cost delta after canary is configured (estimated based on sample traffic profile).
decisions: Variant naming: use 'A'/'B' labels internally, but show full model version string under each variant for clarity (decision logged by Marcus Lee 2025-02-12).
Keep canary ramp presets and allow manual overrides; removed automated ramp schedules from this quickstart to keep complexity low.
Detached the fallback policy editor from the main modal so teams can set complex webhooks in a separate advanced panel (trade-off: more clicks vs cleaner primary flow).
tradeoffs: Simplicity vs control: we prioritize clear first-run UX over exposing every routing knob; advanced controls live in 'Advanced release settings'.
Inline simulation accuracy: preview traffic is approximate and labeled as such to avoid SLA confusion; accurate metrics remain in Observability dashboards.
Localization scope limited to key strings for v1 to meet release date; full translation scheduled for next cycle.
